name.text: NEETUG_PHYSICS_SEMICONDUCTORELECTRONICS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Dynamic resistance behavior in forward and reverse bias

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Beyond the threshold cut-in voltage in forward bias, the diode current increases rapidly with small voltage increments, resulting in a very low dynamic resistance that decreases with increasing forward current.

Statement II: In the reverse bias region prior to breakdown, the dynamic resistance of a silicon p-n junction diode is extremely small and comparable to that of a good metallic conductor.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अग्र अभिनति में देहली (कट-इन) वोल्टता से परे, डायोड धारा में थोड़ी सी वोल्टता वृद्धि के साथ तेजी से वृद्धि होती है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप गतिक प्रतिरोध बहुत कम हो जाता है जो अग्र धारा बढ़ने पर और घटता है।

कथन II: भंजन से पूर्व पश्च अभिनति क्षेत्र में, सिलिकॉन p-n संधि डायोड का गतिक प्रतिरोध अत्यंत कम और एक अच्छे धात्विक चालक के बराबर होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dynamic resistance is defined as the reciprocal of the slope of the \(V\)-\(I\) characteristic curve: \(r_d = \Delta V / \Delta I\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
Above the cut-in voltage (\(\sim 0.7\text{ V}\) for silicon), the forward \(V\)-\(I\) characteristic becomes nearly vertical as current increases exponentially. The differential ratio \(\Delta V / \Delta I\) becomes very small (typically a few ohms to tens of ohms) and decreases as current increases. Therefore, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
In reverse bias before breakdown, current is virtually constant at the reverse saturation level (\(\sim \mu\text{A}\)). Consequently, \(\Delta I / \Delta V\) is nearly zero, meaning dynamic resistance \(r_d = \Delta V / \Delta I\) is extremely large (on the order of megaohms, \(\sim 10^7\text{ }\Omega\)), which is millions of times higher than a metallic conductor. Therefore, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: मूल संकल्पना
गतिक प्रतिरोध \(V\)-\(I\) अभिलक्षण वक्र के ढाल का व्युत्क्रम होता है: \(r_d = \Delta V / \Delta I\)।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
देहली वोल्टता के बाद अग्र धारा तेजी से बढ़ती है, जिससे वक्र का ढाल बहुत अधिक हो जाता है और गतिक प्रतिरोध बहुत कम (कुछ ओम) हो जाता है। अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
भंजन से पहले पश्च अभिनति में धारा लगभग स्थिर रहती है (\(\Delta I \approx 0\)), जिसके कारण गतिक प्रतिरोध अत्यंत उच्च (लगभग \(10^7\text{ }\Omega\)) होता है, न कि धात्विक चालक के समान कम। अतः दूसरा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन सही है, लेकिन दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_PHYSICS_SEMICONDUCTORELECTRONICS_STATEMENT_Q06 - Rectifier conduction half cycles and filter discharge rate

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a simple half-wave rectifier without a filter, load current flows continuously during both the positive and negative half-cycles of the alternating input voltage.

Statement II: In a rectifier circuit equipped with a parallel capacitor filter, the rate of voltage discharge across the capacitor during non-conduction intervals is inversely proportional to the product \(R_L C\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बिना फिल्टर वाले एक साधारण अर्ध-तरंग दिष्टकारी में, निवेशी प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता के धनात्मक और ऋणात्मक दोनों अर्ध-चक्रों के दौरान लोड धारा लगातार प्रवाहित होती है।

कथन II: समांतर संधारित्र फिल्टर से युक्त एक दिष्टकारी परिपथ में, गैर-चालन अंतरालों के दौरान संधारित्र के आर-पार वोल्टता विसर्जन की दर गुणनफल \(R_L C\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A rectifier unidirectionally conducts alternating current, and a filter capacitor smooths pulsating voltage via its discharge time constant.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
A half-wave rectifier uses a single diode that conducts only during the positive half-cycle when forward biased. During the negative half-cycle, it is reverse biased and non-conducting, so load current is zero. Conduction is not continuous. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
When the input AC drops below the peak voltage, the diode ceases conduction and the capacitor discharges through the load resistance \(R_L\). The discharge rate is governed by the time constant \(\tau = R_L C\). A larger \(R_L C\) yields a slower rate of voltage drop across the capacitor. Therefore, the discharge rate is inversely proportional to \(R_L C\), and the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: मूल संकल्पना
दिष्टकारी प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता को एकदिशिक बनाता है तथा संधारित्र विसर्जन समय नियतांक के आधार पर ऊर्मिकाओं को कम करता है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
अर्ध-तरंग दिष्टकारी में डायोड केवल एक अर्ध-चक्र में चालन करता है और दूसरे में बंद रहता है, अतः दोनों अर्ध-चक्रों में लगातार धारा प्रवाहित नहीं होती। इसलिए पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
संधारित्र का विसर्जन समय नियतांक \(\tau = R_L C\) द्वारा निर्धारित होता है। \(R_L C\) जितना बड़ा होगा, विसर्जन की दर उतनी ही धीमी होगी। अतः विसर्जन की दर \(R_L C\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है, और दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन गलत है, लेकिन दूसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_12_SEMICONDUCTOR_ELECTRONICS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Behavior of intrinsic semiconductors and hole conduction

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding intrinsic semiconductors:

Statement I: At absolute zero temperature (0 K), an intrinsic semiconductor acts as a perfect insulator because the valence band is completely filled and the conduction band is completely empty.

Statement II: The apparent motion of a hole in a semiconductor crystal is an effective description of the actual movement of a bound valence electron jumping into an adjacent vacant covalent bond.

Statement III: In an intrinsic semiconductor at room temperature, the equilibrium concentration of free electrons in the conduction band is significantly lower than the concentration of holes in the valence band.

Which of the above statements are correct?

नैज अर्धचालकों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: परम शून्य ताप (0 K) पर, एक नैज अर्धचालक एक आदर्श विद्युतरोधी की भाँति व्यवहार करता है क्योंकि संयोजकता बैंड पूर्णतः भरा होता है और चालन बैंड पूर्णतः रिक्त होता है।

कथन II: एक अर्धचालक क्रिस्टल में होल की आभासी गति वास्तव में एक बद्ध संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉन के निकटवर्ती रिक्त सहसंयोजक बंध में कूदने की वास्तविक गति का एक प्रभावी निरूपण है।

कथन III: कमरे के ताप पर एक नैज अर्धचालक में, चालन बैंड में मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉनों की साम्यावस्था सांद्रता संयोजकता बैंड में होलों की सांद्रता की तुलना में काफी कम होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In an ideal semiconductor at absolute zero (0 K), all valence electrons are locked within covalent bonds, so the valence band is completely filled and the conduction band is completely empty, resulting in zero electrical conductivity. Thermal excitation at non-zero temperatures generates electron-hole pairs in equal numbers, meaning that the intrinsic electron concentration equals the hole concentration (\(n_e = n_h = n_i\)). A hole represents a vacancy left by a liberated valence electron; when an electron from a neighboring covalent bond jumps into this vacancy, the vacancy shifts to the site vacated by that electron, giving the effective appearance of positive charge motion.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
At absolute zero (0 K), thermal energy is insufficient to excite any electrons across the band gap from the valence band into the conduction band. Consequently, the valence band remains completely filled, the conduction band remains completely empty, and no mobile charge carriers are available. Therefore, the material behaves as a perfect insulator. This statement is scientifically accurate and correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Hole conduction occurs purely within the valence band. When a vacancy (hole) exists in a covalent bond, an electron occupying an adjacent bonded state can jump into this vacancy without entering the conduction band. This action fills the initial site and creates a new hole at the adjacent site. Hence, the physical movement of bound valence electrons under an electric field manifests macroscopically as the motion of positive vacancies called holes in the opposite direction. This statement is scientifically accurate and correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
In an intrinsic semiconductor, charge carriers are created exclusively via thermal generation across the band gap. Every single electron promoted to the conduction band leaves behind exactly one vacancy (hole) in the valence band. As a consequence of fundamental charge conservation and pair creation, the electron density must strictly equal the hole density, expressed by the intrinsic equality \(n_e = n_h = n_i\). Therefore, the claim that the electron concentration is significantly lower than the hole concentration is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first statement and the second statement are correct, while the third statement is incorrect. Thus, the correct assessment identifies the first and second statements as the only correct statements.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
परम शून्य ताप (0 K) पर एक आदर्श अर्धचालक में, सभी संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉन सहसंयोजक बंधों में आबंधित होते हैं, अतः संयोजकता बैंड पूर्णतः भरा होता है तथा चालन बैंड पूर्णतः रिक्त होता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप विद्युत चालकता शून्य होती है। अशून्य ताप पर ऊष्मीय उत्तेजन के कारण इलेक्ट्रॉन-होल युग्म समान संख्या में उत्पन्न होते हैं, जिसका अर्थ है कि नैज इलेक्ट्रॉन सांद्रता होल सांद्रता के बराबर होती है (\(n_e = n_h = n_i\))। होल एक मुक्त संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉन द्वारा छोड़ी गई रिक्ति को दर्शाता है; जब किसी निकटवर्ती सहसंयोजक बंध से कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन इस रिक्ति में कूदता है, तो रिक्ति उस इलेक्ट्रॉन के मूल स्थान पर स्थानांतरित हो जाती है, जिससे धनावेश की प्रभावी गति प्रतीत होती है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
परम शून्य ताप (0 K) पर, संयोजकता बैंड से चालन बैंड में ऊर्जा अंतराल को पार कराने के लिए ऊष्मीय ऊर्जा अपर्याप्त होती है। परिणामस्वरूप, संयोजकता बैंड पूर्णतः भरा रहता है, चालन बैंड पूर्णतः रिक्त रहता है और कोई गतिशील आवेश वाहक उपलब्ध नहीं होता है। अतः पदार्थ एक आदर्श विद्युतरोधी की भाँति व्यवहार करता है। यह कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से यथार्थ और सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
होल चालन पूर्णतः संयोजकता बैंड के भीतर होता है। जब किसी सहसंयोजक बंध में एक रिक्ति (होल) उत्पन्न होती है, तो निकटवर्ती बंध में स्थित एक इलेक्ट्रॉन चालन बैंड में जाए बिना इस रिक्ति में कूद सकता है। यह क्रिया प्रारंभिक स्थान को भर देती है और निकटवर्ती स्थान पर एक नया होल उत्पन्न कर देती है। इस प्रकार, विद्युत क्षेत्र के प्रभाव में बद्ध संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉनों की भौतिक गति स्थूल रूप से विपरीत दिशा में गतिशील धनात्मक रिक्तियों (होलों) के रूप में प्रकट होती है। यह कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से यथार्थ और सही है।

चरण 4: तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
एक नैज अर्धचालक में, आवेश वाहक केवल ऊर्जा अंतराल के पार ऊष्मीय जनन के माध्यम से उत्पन्न होते हैं। चालन बैंड में जाने वाला प्रत्येक इलेक्ट्रॉन संयोजकता बैंड में ठीक एक रिक्ति (होल) छोड़ता है। आवेश संरक्षण और युग्म जनन के मूलभूत नियम के अनुसार, इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व सदैव होल घनत्व के ठीक बराबर होना चाहिए, जिसे नैज समानता \(n_e = n_h = n_i\) द्वारा व्यक्त किया जाता है। अतः यह दावा कि इलेक्ट्रॉन सांद्रता होल सांद्रता से काफी कम होती है, गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन और द्वितीय कथन सही हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन गलत है। अतः सही मूल्यांकन केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय कथनों को सही के रूप में पहचानता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_12_SEMICONDUCTOR_ELECTRONICS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Carrier concentrations and energy levels in extrinsic semiconductors

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding extrinsic semiconductors in thermal equilibrium:

Statement I: In an n-type semiconductor, the donor energy level lies just below the bottom of the conduction band, allowing electrons to be thermally ionized into the conduction band at room temperature.

Statement II: According to the law of mass action, the product of electron and hole concentrations in an extrinsic semiconductor in thermal equilibrium is independent of the doping concentration and equals \(n_i^2\).

Statement III: An n-type semiconductor acquires a net negative electrostatic charge due to the abundance of free conduction electrons donated by pentavalent impurity atoms.

Which of the above statements are correct?

ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालकों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: एक n-प्रकार के अर्धचालक में, दाता ऊर्जा स्तर चालन बैंड के निचले सिरे के ठीक नीचे स्थित होता है, जिससे कमरे के ताप पर इलेक्ट्रॉन ऊष्मीय रूप से आयनित होकर चालन बैंड में जा सकते हैं।

कथन II: द्रव्य अनुपाती क्रिया के नियम के अनुसार, ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में एक अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक में इलेक्ट्रॉन और होल सांद्रताओं का गुणनफल अपमिश्रण सांद्रता पर निर्भर नहीं करता है और \(n_i^2\) के बराबर होता है।

कथन III: पंचसंयोजी अपद्रव्य परमाणुओं द्वारा दिए गए मुक्त चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की प्रचुरता के कारण एक n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक कुल ऋणात्मक स्थिरवैद्युत आवेश प्राप्त कर लेता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In extrinsic semiconductors, doping creates localized discrete energy levels within the forbidden band gap. Pentavalent dopants create donor levels \(E_D\) just below the conduction band edge \(E_C\), typically \(\approx 0.01\text{ eV}\) to \(0.05\text{ eV}\) below \(E_C\). In thermal equilibrium at temperature \(T\), the product of electron concentration \(n_e\) and hole concentration \(n_h\) obeys the mass-action law \(n_e n_h = n_i^2(T)\), which depends strictly on the band gap and temperature but is independent of the dopant concentration. Furthermore, donor atoms are electrically neutral before ionization; upon releasing an electron into the conduction band, the donor atom becomes a fixed positive ion, ensuring that the macroscopic crystal remains strictly electrically neutral.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
Pentavalent impurities introduce extra valence electrons that are very loosely bound to the impurity atoms. The energetic state of these fifth electrons lies in a discrete donor level \(E_D\) located just below the conduction band edge \(E_C\). Because the required ionization energy is minuscule (\(\approx 0.01\text{ eV}\) in germanium and \(\approx 0.05\text{ eV}\) in silicon), room temperature thermal energy (\(k_B T \approx 0.026\text{ eV}\)) easily excites virtually all these donor electrons into the conduction band. This statement is scientifically accurate and correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
In any semiconductor in thermal equilibrium, the generation rate of electron-hole pairs equals the recombination rate. Recombination occurs when an electron meets a hole, making the recombination rate proportional to the product \(n_e n_h\). At steady-state thermal equilibrium, this product is governed strictly by the intrinsic carrier concentration at that temperature, \(n_e n_h = n_i^2\). Introducing donor or acceptor dopants suppresses minority carriers via enhanced recombination such that their product remains fixed at \(n_i^2\), irrespective of dopant density. This statement is scientifically accurate and correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Although free conduction electrons outnumber holes in an n-type semiconductor, each donated mobile electron leaves behind a fixed, positively charged donor ion in the crystal lattice. The total density of negative charges (conduction electrons and ionized acceptors) precisely balances the total density of positive charges (holes and ionized donor cores), fulfilling the charge neutrality condition \(n_e + N_A^- = n_h + N_D^+\). Thus, the net electrostatic charge of an n-type semiconductor crystal is strictly zero, and it does not acquire any net negative charge. This statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first statement and the second statement are correct, while the third statement is incorrect. Thus, the correct assessment identifies the first and second statements as the only correct statements.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालकों में, अपमिश्रण वर्जित ऊर्जा अंतराल के भीतर विविक्त ऊर्जा स्तर उत्पन्न करता है। पंचसंयोजी अपद्रव्य चालन बैंड के किनारे \(E_C\) के ठीक नीचे दाता स्तर \(E_D\) बनाते हैं, जो सामान्यतः \(E_C\) से लगभग \(0.01\text{ eV}\) से \(0.05\text{ eV}\) नीचे होता है। ताप \(T\) पर ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में, इलेक्ट्रॉन सांद्रता \(n_e\) और होल सांद्रता \(n_h\) का गुणनफल द्रव्य अनुपाती क्रिया के नियम \(n_e n_h = n_i^2(T)\) का पालन करता है, जो केवल ऊर्जा अंतराल और ताप पर निर्भर करता है तथा अपमिश्रक सांद्रता से स्वतंत्र होता है। इसके अतिरिक्त, आयनीकरण से पूर्व दाता परमाणु विद्युत उदासीन होते हैं; चालन बैंड में इलेक्ट्रॉन देने के बाद दाता परमाणु एक स्थिर धनात्मक आयन बन जाता है, जिससे संपूर्ण क्रिस्टल पूर्णतः विद्युत उदासीन बना रहता है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
पंचसंयोजी अपद्रव्य अतिरिक्त संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉन लाते हैं जो अपद्रव्य परमाणुओं से बहुत दुर्बल रूप से बंधे होते हैं। इन पाँचवें इलेक्ट्रॉनों की ऊर्जा अवस्था चालन बैंड के किनारे \(E_C\) के ठीक नीचे एक विविक्त दाता स्तर \(E_D\) में स्थित होती है। चूँकि आवश्यक आयनन ऊर्जा अत्यंत सूक्ष्म होती है (जर्मेनियम में लगभग \(0.01\text{ eV}\) तथा सिलिकॉन में लगभग \(0.05\text{ eV}\)), अतः कमरे के ताप पर ऊष्मीय ऊर्जा (\(k_B T \approx 0.026\text{ eV}\)) इन सभी दाता इलेक्ट्रॉनों को आसानी से चालन बैंड में उत्तेजित कर देती है। यह कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से यथार्थ और सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में किसी भी अर्धचालक में, इलेक्ट्रॉन-होल युग्मों की जनन दर उनके पुनर्संयोजन दर के बराबर होती है। पुनर्संयोजन तब होता है जब एक इलेक्ट्रॉन एक होल से मिलता है, जिससे पुनर्संयोजन दर गुणनफल \(n_e n_h\) के समानुपाती होती है। स्थायी ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में, यह गुणनफल उस ताप पर केवल नैज वाहक सांद्रता द्वारा निर्धारित होता है, अर्थात् \(n_e n_h = n_i^2\)। दाता या ग्राही अपद्रव्य मिलाने से तीव्र पुनर्संयोजन के कारण अल्पसंख्यक वाहक कम हो जाते हैं जिससे उनका गुणनफल अपमिश्रक घनत्व से स्वतंत्र होकर \(n_i^2\) पर स्थिर रहता है। यह कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से यथार्थ और सही है।

चरण 4: तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
यद्यपि n-प्रकार के अर्धचालक में मुक्त चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या होलों से अधिक होती है, परंतु प्रत्येक दिया गया गतिशील इलेक्ट्रॉन क्रिस्टल जालक में एक स्थिर धनावेशित दाता आयन छोड़ता है। ऋणात्मक आवेशों (चालन इलेक्ट्रॉन और आयनित ग्राही) का कुल घनत्व धनात्मक आवेशों (होल और आयनित दाता कोर) के कुल घनत्व को पूर्णतः संतुलित करता है, जो आवेश उदासीनता प्रतिबंध \(n_e + N_A^- = n_h + N_D^+\) को संतुष्ट करता है। अतः n-प्रकार के अर्धचालक क्रिस्टल का कुल स्थिरवैद्युत आवेश पूर्णतः शून्य होता है, और यह कोई कुल ऋणात्मक आवेश प्राप्त नहीं करता है। यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन और द्वितीय कथन सही हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन गलत है। अतः सही मूल्यांकन केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय कथनों को सही के रूप में पहचानता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS_12_SEMICONDUCTOR_ELECTRONICS_STATEMENT_Q03 - Biasing mechanics and rectification in junction diodes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding p-n junction diodes and rectification circuits:

Statement I: Under reverse bias, the applied voltage aligns with the direction of the built-in barrier field, widening the depletion region and limiting the current to a very small minority-carrier drift current that is nearly independent of the reverse voltage until breakdown.

Statement II: In a full-wave rectifier supplied by an alternating input voltage of frequency \(\nu\), each diode conducts alternately during opposite half-cycles, resulting in a rectified output containing a fundamental ripple frequency of \(2\nu\).

Statement III: Adding a parallel shunt capacitor filter across the load resistor in a rectifier circuit increases the output AC ripple voltage because the capacitor periodically discharges energy directly into the AC source.

Which of the above statements are correct?

p-n संधि डायोड और दिष्टकारी परिपथों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: पश्च अभिनति के अंतर्गत, आरोपित वोल्टता आंतरिक प्राचीर क्षेत्र की दिशा में संरेखित होती है, जिससे अवक्षय क्षेत्र चौड़ा हो जाता है और धारा एक अत्यंत सूक्ष्म अल्पसंख्यक-वाहक अपवाह धारा तक सीमित हो जाती है जो भंजन तक पश्च वोल्टता से लगभग स्वतंत्र रहती है।

कथन II: \(\nu\) आवृत्ति की प्रत्यावर्ती निवेशी वोल्टता द्वारा आपूर्ति किए जाने वाले एक पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी में, प्रत्येक डायोड बारी-बारी से विपरीत अर्ध-चक्रों के दौरान चालन करता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप प्राप्त दिष्टकृत निर्गत में \(2\nu\) की मूलभूत ऊर्मिका आवृत्ति होती है।

कथन III: एक दिष्टकारी परिपथ में लोड प्रतिरोध के सिरों पर एक समानांतर शंट संधारित्र फिल्टर जोड़ने से निर्गत प्रत्यावर्ती ऊर्मिका वोल्टता बढ़ जाती है क्योंकि संधारित्र समय-समय पर सीधे प्रत्यावर्ती स्रोत में ऊर्जा विसर्जित करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The analysis concerns a semiconductor p-n junction under reverse bias and a full-wave rectifier circuit with a smoothing capacitor filter. An input AC signal has fundamental frequency \(\nu\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Physical Principles
In a p-n junction, the built-in electric field points from the n-side (positive donor cores) to the p-side (negative acceptor cores). In reverse bias, the external battery terminal connects positive to the n-region and negative to the p-region, reinforcing the internal barrier field. In rectification, a full-wave configuration rectifies both positive and negative half-cycles of the AC cycle of period \(T = 1/\nu\). Shunt capacitor filtering utilizes the electrostatic charge storage of the capacitor across the load.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Circuit Relations
The total junction barrier potential in reverse bias is \(V_0 + V_R\), where \(V_R\) is the reverse bias magnitude. The reverse saturation current is determined by thermally generated minority carriers: \(I_s \propto \left(\frac{D_p p_n}{L_p} + \frac{D_n n_p}{L_n}\right)\). For a full-wave rectifier, output pulses occur twice per input cycle, giving an output repetition period \(T_{\text{out}} = T/2\), corresponding to a fundamental ripple frequency \(\nu_{\text{out}} = 2\nu\). With a parallel capacitor filter, the ripple voltage is approximately \(V_r = \frac{I_{\text{dc}}}{2\nu C}\), which is inversely proportional to capacitance \(C\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Evaluation of Statements
Evaluation of the First Statement: In reverse bias, the applied voltage has the same polarity as the built-in potential, so the net barrier height increases to \(V_0 + V_R\) and the depletion layer expands. Majority carrier diffusion across the barrier is completely blocked. Only minority carriers (thermally generated electrons in the p-side and holes in the n-side) that wander into the depletion zone are swept across by the strong electric field. Because their generation rate depends solely on temperature and material band gap (not on the magnitude of the applied reverse voltage), this reverse drift current rapidly saturates to a tiny constant value \(I_s\) (microamperes in Ge, nanoamperes in Si) until avalanche or Zener breakdown occurs. Thus, this statement is correct.
Evaluation of the Second Statement: In a full-wave rectifier (whether centre-tapped or bridge configuration), one diode conducts during the positive half-cycle and the other diode conducts during the negative half-cycle. Both half-cycles produce unidirectional current pulses across the load in the exact same direction. Consequently, two positive pulses appear across the load for every single full cycle of the input wave. The output waveform repeats every \(T/2\) seconds, which means its fundamental repetition frequency (ripple frequency) is \(\nu_{\text{out}} = \frac{1}{T/2} = 2\nu\). Thus, this statement is correct.
Evaluation of the Third Statement: A shunt capacitor connected in parallel with the load resistor charges to the peak voltage \(V_m\) when a diode conducts. When the rectified input drops below the capacitor voltage, the diode becomes reverse-biased, isolating the capacitor and load from the AC source. The capacitor then slowly discharges its stored charge exclusively through the load resistor with a time constant \(\tau = R_L C\), holding the load voltage near \(V_m\) until the next cycle's peak arrives. It does not discharge back into the source, and this action significantly reduces the ripple voltage rather than increasing it. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The first statement and the second statement are physically valid and correct, while the third statement contradicts the fundamental smoothing action of a parallel capacitor filter. Therefore, the correct assessment identifies the first and second statements as the only correct statements.

चरण 1: दिए गए आँकड़े और स्थितियाँ
यह विश्लेषण पश्च अभिनति के अंतर्गत एक अर्धचालक p-n संधि और एक संधारित्र फिल्टर युक्त पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी परिपथ से संबंधित है। निवेशी प्रत्यावर्ती संकेत की मूलभूत आवृत्ति \(\nu\) है।

चरण 2: मान्यताएँ और भौतिक सिद्धांत
p-n संधि में, आंतरिक विद्युत क्षेत्र n-क्षेत्र (धनात्मक दाता कोर) से p-क्षेत्र (ऋणात्मक ग्राही कोर) की ओर दिष्ट होता है। पश्च अभिनति में, बाह्य बैटरी का धनात्मक सिरा n-क्षेत्र से और ऋणात्मक सिरा p-क्षेत्र से जुड़ता है, जिससे आंतरिक प्राचीर क्षेत्र सुदृढ़ होता है। दिष्टकरण में, एक पूर्ण-तरंग विन्यास आवर्तकाल \(T = 1/\nu\) वाले प्रत्यावर्ती चक्र के दोनों धनात्मक और ऋणात्मक अर्ध-चक्रों को दिष्टकृत करता है। शंट संधारित्र फिल्टरिंग लोड के सिरों पर संधारित्र के स्थिरवैद्युत आवेश भंडारण का उपयोग करती है।

चरण 3: संबंधित सूत्र और परिपथ संबंध
पश्च अभिनति में कुल संधि प्राचीर विभव \(V_0 + V_R\) होता है, जहाँ \(V_R\) पश्च अभिनति का मान है। संतृप्ति पश्च धारा ऊष्मीय रूप से जनित अल्पसंख्यक वाहकों द्वारा निर्धारित होती है: \(I_s \propto \left(\frac{D_p p_n}{L_p} + \frac{D_n n_p}{L_n}\right)\)। पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी के लिए, प्रति निवेशी चक्र में दो बार निर्गत स्पंद प्राप्त होते हैं, जिससे निर्गत पुनरावृत्ति काल \(T_{\text{out}} = T/2\) प्राप्त होता है, जो मूलभूत ऊर्मिका आवृत्ति \(\nu_{\text{out}} = 2\nu\) के संगत है। समानांतर संधारित्र फिल्टर के साथ, ऊर्मिका वोल्टता लगभग \(V_r = \frac{I_{\text{dc}}}{2\nu C}\) होती है, जो धारिता \(C\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

चरण 4: कथनों का चरण-दर-चरण मूल्यांकन
प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन: पश्च अभिनति में, आरोपित वोल्टता की ध्रुवता आंतरिक विभव के समान होती है, अतः कुल प्राचीर ऊँचाई बढ़कर \(V_0 + V_R\) हो जाती है तथा अवक्षय परत चौड़ी हो जाती है। प्राचीर के पार बहुसंख्यक वाहकों का विसरण पूर्णतः रुक जाता है। केवल वे अल्पसंख्यक वाहक (p-क्षेत्र में ऊष्मीय रूप से जनित इलेक्ट्रॉन और n-क्षेत्र में होल) जो अवक्षय क्षेत्र में पहुँचते हैं, प्रबल विद्युत क्षेत्र द्वारा त्वरित होकर पार कर जाते हैं। चूँकि उनकी जनन दर केवल ताप और ऊर्जा अंतराल पर निर्भर करती है (आरोपित पश्च वोल्टता के परिमाण पर नहीं), इसलिए यह पश्च अपवाह धारा तेजी से एक सूक्ष्म नियत मान \(I_s\) (Ge में माइक्रोएम्पीयर, Si में नैनोएम्पीयर) पर संतृप्त हो जाती है जब तक कि एवलांश या जेनर भंजन न हो जाए। अतः यह कथन सही है।
द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन: एक पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी में (चाहे मध्य-निष्कासित ट्रांसफार्मर हो या ब्रिज विन्यास), धनात्मक अर्ध-चक्र के दौरान एक डायोड चालन करता है और ऋणात्मक अर्ध-चक्र के दौरान दूसरा डायोड चालन करता है। दोनों अर्ध-चक्र लोड के सिरों पर ठीक एक ही दिशा में एकदिशीय धारा स्पंद उत्पन्न करते हैं। परिणामस्वरूप, निवेशी तरंग के प्रत्येक एक पूर्ण चक्र के लिए लोड पर दो धनात्मक स्पंद प्रकट होते हैं। निर्गत तरंगरूप प्रत्येक \(T/2\) सेकंड में दोहराता है, जिसका अर्थ है कि इसकी मूलभूत पुनरावृत्ति आवृत्ति (ऊर्मिका आवृत्ति) \(\nu_{\text{out}} = \frac{1}{T/2} = 2\nu\) होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।
तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन: लोड प्रतिरोध के समानांतर जुड़ा एक शंट संधारित्र किसी डायोड के चालन के समय शिखर वोल्टता \(V_m\) तक आवेशित हो जाता है। जब दिष्टकृत निवेश संधारित्र वोल्टता से कम हो जाता है, तो डायोड पश्च-अभिनत हो जाता है, जिससे संधारित्र और लोड प्रत्यावर्ती स्रोत से विलग हो जाते हैं। तब संधारित्र अपने संचित आवेश को समय नियतांक \(\tau = R_L C\) के साथ केवल लोड प्रतिरोध के माध्यम से धीरे-धीरे विसर्जित करता है, जिससे अगले चक्र के शिखर आने तक लोड वोल्टता \(V_m\) के निकट बनी रहती है। यह स्रोत में वापस विसर्जित नहीं होता है, और यह क्रिया ऊर्मिका वोल्टता को बढ़ाने के बजाय काफी कम कर देती है। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 5: जाँच और अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन और द्वितीय कथन भौतिक रूप से वैध और सही हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन समानांतर संधारित्र फिल्टर की मूलभूत समकारी क्रिया का खंडन करता है। अतः सही मूल्यांकन केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय कथनों को सही के रूप में पहचानता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Classification of solids and semiconductors

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Metals (Conductors) I. Forbidden energy band gap \(E_g > 3\text{ eV}\) (e.g., Diamond with \(5.4\text{ eV}\))
B. Elemental Semiconductors II. Conduction band overlaps valence band or band gap is zero (\(E_g \approx 0\))
C. Insulators III. Compound semiconductors such as CdS and GaAs
D. Inorganic Compound Semiconductors IV. Silicon (Si) and Germanium (Ge) with narrow band gaps (\(0.2\text{ eV} < E_g < 3\text{ eV}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Solids are classified into metals, semiconductors, and insulators based on their energy band structures, forbidden energy gaps (\(E_g\)), and elemental or compound chemical composition.

Step-by-Step Item Matching:
Evaluating each item in Column I with its appropriate description in Column II:
• Metals (Conductors): Characterized by an overlapping conduction and valence band where \(E_g \approx 0\), allowing free movement of valence electrons. Thus, item A matches description II.
• Elemental Semiconductors: Composed of pure Group 14 elements Si and Ge having small, finite band gaps (\(E_g \approx 1.1\text{ eV}\) for Si and \(E_g \approx 0.7\text{ eV}\) for Ge). Thus, item B matches description IV.
• Insulators: Possess a very wide forbidden energy gap (\(E_g > 3\text{ eV}\), e.g., diamond with \(E_g \approx 5.4\text{ eV}\)) that prevents thermal promotion of electrons into the conduction band at ordinary temperatures. Thus, item C matches description I.
• Inorganic Compound Semiconductors: Formed by combinations of inorganic elements such as cadmium sulphide (CdS) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Thus, item D matches description III.

Check and Final Answer:
Combining the individual pairings yields the overall mapping: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Doping impurities and extrinsic semiconductor properties

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Pentavalent dopant (Donor impurity) I. Introduces an acceptor energy level \(E_A\) slightly above the valence band
B. Trivalent dopant (Acceptor impurity) II. Introduces a donor energy level \(E_D\) slightly below the conduction band
C. \(n\)-type semiconductor III. Mobile holes are majority carriers (\(n_h \gg n_e\)) with bulk crystal charge neutrality
D. \(p\)-type semiconductor IV. Conduction electrons are majority carriers (\(n_e \gg n_h\)) with bulk crystal charge neutrality

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Extrinsic semiconductors are created by adding specific trivalent or pentavalent impurity dopants to pure tetravalent crystals, which creates localized impurity energy levels and alters majority and minority carrier populations while conserving electrical neutrality.

Step-by-Step Item Matching:
Evaluating each item in Column I with its appropriate description in Column II:
• Pentavalent dopant (Donor impurity): Elements like phosphorus, arsenic, or antimony provide extra electrons bound by small ionization energies (\(\sim 0.01\text{ to } 0.05\text{ eV}\)), creating donor energy states \(E_D\) located just below the conduction band edge \(E_C\). Thus, item A matches description II.
• Trivalent dopant (Acceptor impurity): Elements like boron, aluminum, or indium create vacancies (holes) that easily capture valence electrons, creating acceptor energy states \(E_A\) located just above the valence band edge \(E_V\). Thus, item B matches description I.
• \(n\)-type semiconductor: Pentavalent doping causes electrons to vastly outnumber holes (\(n_e \gg n_h\)), yet the positive donor ions exactly balance excess electron charges, keeping the bulk crystal electrically neutral. Thus, item C matches description IV.
• \(p\)-type semiconductor: Trivalent doping causes holes to vastly outnumber electrons (\(n_h \gg n_e\)), yet the negative acceptor ions balance the mobile holes, preserving overall electrical neutrality. Thus, item D matches description III.

Check and Final Answer:
Combining the individual pairings yields the overall mapping: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Operating states and characteristics of semiconductor devices

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Column I Column II
A. Unbiased \(p\text{-}n\) junction at equilibrium I. Barrier height rises to \((V_0 + V)\), widening depletion layer with tiny minority carrier drift current
B. Forward biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction II. Barrier height falls to \((V_0 - V)\), narrowing depletion layer with heavy minority carrier injection in mA
C. Reverse biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction III. Forward diffusion current exactly balances reverse drift current, producing zero net current
D. Full-wave rectifier with capacitor filter IV. Converts both half-cycles into unidirectional pulses whose discharge rate across \(R_L\) is governed by time constant \(C R_L\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The electrical response of a \(p\text{-}n\) junction depends directly on the polarity of the applied bias, which modulates the built-in barrier potential, changes the depletion layer width, and alters carrier transport, while filtering smoothing circuits rely on capacitive time constants.

Step-by-Step Item Matching:
Evaluating each item in Column I with its appropriate description in Column II:
• Unbiased \(p\text{-}n\) junction at equilibrium: At equilibrium without bias, the forward diffusion of majority carriers across the concentration gradient is dynamically and exactly cancelled by the drift of minority carriers under the built-in electric field, resulting in strictly zero net current across the junction. Thus, item A matches description III.
• Forward biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction: When the \(p\)-side is connected to the positive terminal and \(n\)-side to the negative terminal, the applied voltage opposes the built-in barrier potential, reducing the barrier to \((V_0 - V)\) and narrowing the depletion region. This enables significant minority carrier injection that yields a forward diffusion current measured in milliamperes. Thus, item B matches description II.
• Reverse biased \(p\text{-}n\) junction: When the \(n\)-side is made positive and \(p\)-side negative, the external voltage aids the built-in field, raising the potential barrier to \((V_0 + V)\) and widening the depletion layer. Majority diffusion is suppressed, leaving only a minute drift current (saturation current) of thermally generated minority carriers measured in microamperes. Thus, item C matches description I.
• Full-wave rectifier with capacitor filter: In a full-wave rectifier, both positive and negative input half-cycles conduct through alternate diodes in the identical direction across the load resistor. The parallel capacitor charges to peak voltage during conduction and discharges through the load resistor with an exponential decay rate dictated by time constant \(\tau = C R_L\). Thus, item D matches description IV.

Check and Final Answer:
Combining the individual pairings yields the overall mapping: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Ripple frequency of full wave rectifier circuit

questiontext.text: An alternating sinusoidal voltage with a mains frequency of \(60\text{ Hz}\) is connected to the primary of a transformer supplying a centre-tapped full-wave rectifier. What is the fundamental ripple frequency of the output voltage across the load resistor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Input ac supply frequency: \(f_{\text{in}} = 60\text{ Hz}\). Rectifier type: centre-tapped full-wave rectifier.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard full-wave rectification where both positive and negative half-cycles produce output pulses across the load resistor in the same direction.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
In a full-wave rectifier, two output conduction pulses occur for each complete cycle of the input ac voltage wave. Therefore, the output ripple frequency is twice the input frequency: \[ f_{\text{out}} = 2 f_{\text{in}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given frequency: \[ f_{\text{out}} = 2 \times 60\text{ Hz} = 120\text{ Hz} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are hertz (\(\text{Hz}\)). For half-wave rectification the output frequency equals the input frequency (\(60\text{ Hz}\)), whereas for full-wave rectification it is doubled to \(120\text{ Hz}\).

Final Answer: The fundamental ripple frequency of the full-wave rectifier output is \(120\text{ Hz}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Total current calculation in intrinsic semiconductor

questiontext.text: In an intrinsic semiconductor under the influence of an external electric field, the conduction electron current is measured to be \(I_e = 4.2\ \mu\text{A}\) and the hole current is measured to be \(I_h = 1.8\ \mu\text{A}\). What is the total electric current \(I\) flowing through the semiconductor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Electron current component: \(I_e = 4.2\ \mu\text{A}\). Hole current component: \(I_h = 1.8\ \mu\text{A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Conduction electrons drift opposite to the applied electric field while holes drift along the electric field. Since conventional current due to both negative electrons and positive holes is directed in the direction of the electric field, both currents contribute additively.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total current \(I\) in a semiconductor is the scalar sum of the electron current and hole current: \[ I = I_e + I_h \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the equation: \[ I = 4.2\ \mu\text{A} + 1.8\ \mu\text{A} = 6.0\ \mu\text{A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are microamperes (\(\mu\text{A}\)). The total current correctly exceeds each individual component and satisfies conservation of charge.

Final Answer: The total electric current flowing through the semiconductor is \(6.0\ \mu\text{A}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Effective barrier potential under forward bias

questiontext.text: A silicon p-n junction diode has an equilibrium built-in barrier potential of \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\). When an external forward bias voltage of \(V = 0.45\text{ V}\) is applied across the terminals, what is the effective barrier height across the depletion region?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Built-in barrier potential at equilibrium: \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\). Applied forward bias voltage: \(V = 0.45\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Under forward bias, the positive battery terminal connects to the p-side and the negative terminal connects to the n-side, opposing the internal junction electric field.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The applied forward voltage drops across the high-resistance depletion layer in opposition to the built-in potential, reducing the barrier height to: \[ V_{\text{eff}} = V_0 - V \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values: \[ V_{\text{eff}} = 0.70\text{ V} - 0.45\text{ V} = 0.25\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are volts (\(\text{V}\)). The barrier height is lowered from \(0.70\text{ V}\) to \(0.25\text{ V}\), which facilitates majority carrier injection.

Final Answer: The effective barrier height across the depletion region under forward bias is \(0.25\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Dynamic resistance of forward biased silicon diode

questiontext.text: During a laboratory experiment on a forward-biased silicon diode, the voltage across the diode is increased from \(0.65\text{ V}\) to \(0.75\text{ V}\). In response, the forward current increases from \(5.0\text{ mA}\) to \(25.0\text{ mA}\). What is the dynamic resistance of the diode in this region?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial forward voltage: \(V_1 = 0.65\text{ V}\), final forward voltage: \(V_2 = 0.75\text{ V}\). Initial current: \(I_1 = 5.0\text{ mA}\), final current: \(I_2 = 25.0\text{ mA}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The diode operates in its forward conduction characteristic where dynamic resistance is defined by small-signal increments.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Dynamic resistance \(r_d\) is defined as the ratio of an incremental change in voltage to the resulting incremental change in current: \[ r_d = \frac{\Delta V}{\Delta I} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute the change in voltage: \[ \Delta V = V_2 - V_1 = 0.75\text{ V} - 0.65\text{ V} = 0.10\text{ V} \] Compute the change in current: \[ \Delta I = I_2 - I_1 = 25.0\text{ mA} - 5.0\text{ mA} = 20.0\text{ mA} = 20.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A} = 0.020\text{ A} \] Calculate dynamic resistance: \[ r_d = \frac{0.10\text{ V}}{0.020\text{ A}} = 5.0\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are ohms (\(\Omega\)). A dynamic resistance of \(5.0\ \Omega\) is physically realistic for a conducting silicon diode above its cut-in threshold.

Final Answer: The dynamic resistance of the diode is \(5.0\ \Omega\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q05 - Equilibrium hole density in arsenic doped silicon

questiontext.text: A pure silicon sample with an intrinsic carrier concentration of \(n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3}\) is doped with arsenic atoms. If the resulting majority electron density is \(n_e = 4.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3}\), what is the equilibrium minority hole density in the crystal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Intrinsic carrier concentration: \(n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3}\). Majority electron concentration: \(n_e = 4.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Thermal equilibrium is maintained, and complete ionization of donor impurities is assumed at room temperature.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to the law of mass action in a semiconductor under thermal equilibrium: \[ n_e n_h = n_i^2 \implies n_h = \frac{n_i^2}{n_e} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \(n_i^2\): \[ n_i^2 = (1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3})^2 = 2.25 \times 10^{32}\text{ m}^{-6} \] Calculate the hole concentration \(n_h\): \[ n_h = \frac{2.25 \times 10^{32}\text{ m}^{-6}}{4.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3}} = 0.50 \times 10^{10}\text{ m}^{-3} = 5.0 \times 10^9\text{ m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are \(\text{m}^{-3}\). Check the mass action product: \((4.5 \times 10^{22}) \times (5.0 \times 10^9) = 22.5 \times 10^{31} = 2.25 \times 10^{32} = n_i^2\). The value is completely consistent.

Final Answer: The equilibrium minority hole density is \(5.0 \times 10^{9}\text{ m}^{-3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q06 - Average electric field in depletion layer calculation

questiontext.text: In an unbiased p-n junction diode, the barrier potential across the depletion layer is \(V_0 = 0.60\text{ V}\) and the thickness of the depletion layer is \(0.20\ \\mu\\text{m}\). What is the magnitude of the average electric field established across the depletion layer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Barrier potential difference: \(V_0 = 0.60\text{ V}\). Depletion layer width: \(W = 0.20\ \mu\text{m} = 0.20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The electric field points from the positive space-charge region (n-side) to the negative space-charge region (p-side). The average electric field magnitude is determined across the layer.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The average electric field \(E_{\text{avg}}\) across a potential difference \(V_0\) over a distance \(W\) is given by: \[ E_{\text{avg}} = \frac{V_0}{W} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical values: \[ E_{\text{avg}} = \frac{0.60\text{ V}}{0.20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}} = 3.0 \times 10^6\text{ V m}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are volts per metre (\(\text{V m}^{-1}\)). An electric field of order \(10^6\text{ V m}^{-1}\) is typical of semiconductor p-n junctions due to sub-micrometre depletion widths.

Final Answer: The magnitude of the average electric field is \(3.0 \times 10^6\text{ V m}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q07 - Minority electron density in indium doped silicon

questiontext.text: A sample of silicon with intrinsic concentration \(n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3}\) is doped with trivalent indium atoms to produce a majority hole concentration of \(n_h = 2.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3}\). What is the concentration of minority conduction electrons at thermal equilibrium?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Intrinsic carrier concentration: \(n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3}\). Majority hole concentration: \(n_h = 2.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The semiconductor is in thermal equilibrium at room temperature, satisfying the mass action law.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By the law of mass action: \[ n_e n_h = n_i^2 \implies n_e = \frac{n_i^2}{n_h} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \(n_i^2\): \[ n_i^2 = (1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3})^2 = 2.25 \times 10^{32}\text{ m}^{-6} \] Calculate the electron concentration: \[ n_e = \frac{2.25 \times 10^{32}\text{ m}^{-6}}{2.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3}} = 0.90 \times 10^{10}\text{ m}^{-3} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are \(\text{m}^{-3}\). Check the product: \((9.0 \times 10^9) \times (2.5 \times 10^{22}) = 22.5 \times 10^{31} = 2.25 \times 10^{32} = n_i^2\). The value is confirmed.

Final Answer: The minority conduction electron concentration is \(9.0 \times 10^{9}\text{ m}^{-3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q08 - Reverse static resistance of pn junction diode

questiontext.text: When a reverse bias voltage of \(V = -8.0\text{ V}\) is applied across a junction diode, a reverse saturation current of \(I = -0.50\ \mu\text{A}\) is observed. What is the static electrical resistance offered by the diode under this reverse bias condition?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Applied reverse bias voltage: \(V = -8.0\text{ V}\). Reverse current: \(I = -0.50\ \mu\text{A} = -0.50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Static resistance is defined from Ohm's law as the ratio of the magnitude of applied voltage to the magnitude of the resulting current at the specified operating point.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Static reverse resistance: \[ R_{rb} = \frac{|V|}{|I|} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical magnitudes: \[ R_{rb} = \frac{8.0\text{ V}}{0.50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ A}} = 16 \times 10^6\ \Omega = 1.6 \times 10^7\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are ohms (\(\Omega\)). A value of \(16\text{ M}\Omega\) is consistent with the high resistance presented by reverse-biased semiconductor junctions.

Final Answer: The static reverse resistance of the diode is \(1.6 \times 10^7\ \Omega\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q09 - Peak load current in halfwave rectifier calculation

questiontext.text: A half-wave rectifier circuit consists of a transformer secondary delivering a sinusoidal peak voltage of \(V_m = 15.7\text{ V}\) in series with a silicon diode and a load resistor of \(R_L = 500\ \Omega\). Assuming the diode has a constant cut-in voltage drop of \(0.70\text{ V}\) during conduction and negligible forward resistance, what is the peak current through the load resistor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Peak input ac voltage: \(V_m = 15.7\text{ V}\). Diode cut-in potential drop: \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\). Load resistance: \(R_L = 500\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The diode conducts during the positive half-cycle when the applied voltage exceeds \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\). Its forward dynamic resistance is taken as zero during conduction.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law across the series loop at the peak of the input cycle: \[ V_m - V_0 - I_{\text{peak}} R_L = 0 \implies I_{\text{peak}} = \frac{V_m - V_0}{R_L} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the peak voltage across the load resistor: \[ V_{L,\text{peak}} = V_m - V_0 = 15.7\text{ V} - 0.70\text{ V} = 15.0\text{ V} \] Compute the peak current: \[ I_{\text{peak}} = \frac{15.0\text{ V}}{500\ \Omega} = 0.030\text{ A} = 30.0\text{ mA} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are milliamperes (\(\text{mA}\)). Accounting for the \(0.70\text{ V}\) junction drop gives \(30.0\text{ mA}\), whereas an ideal zero-drop model would yield \(31.4\text{ mA}\).

Final Answer: The peak current flowing through the load resistor is \(30.0\text{ mA}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q10 - Time constant of rectifier capacitor filter circuit

questiontext.text: In a dc power supply, a full-wave rectifier uses a capacitor filter with capacitance \(C = 220\ \mu\text{F}\) connected in parallel with a load resistor \(R_L = 500\ \Omega\). What is the discharge time constant of this capacitor filter?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Filter capacitance: \(C = 220\ \mu\text{F} = 220 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}\). Effective load resistance: \(R_L = 500\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
When the rectifier diodes cease conduction after charging the capacitor to peak voltage, the capacitor discharges exponentially through the load resistance \(R_L\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The discharge time constant \(\tau\) of a parallel \(R_L C\) filter circuit is given by: \[ \tau = R_L C \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply resistance by capacitance: \[ \tau = 500\ \Omega \times (220 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}) = 110000 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s} = 0.110\text{ s} = 110\text{ ms} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are milliseconds (\(\text{ms}\)). For a \(50\text{ Hz}\) full-wave rectifier with a pulse period of \(10\text{ ms}\), a time constant of \(110\text{ ms}\) is significantly greater than \(10\text{ ms}\), which successfully provides effective filtering.

Final Answer: The discharge time constant of the capacitor filter is \(110\text{ ms}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q11 - Effective barrier potential under reverse bias voltage

questiontext.text: A semiconductor diode has an equilibrium built-in barrier potential of \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\). If an external reverse bias voltage of \(V = 5.30\text{ V}\) is applied across the diode terminals, what is the effective barrier height opposing majority carrier diffusion across the junction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Equilibrium built-in barrier potential: \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\). Applied reverse bias voltage: \(V = 5.30\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In reverse bias, the positive terminal of the external battery is connected to the n-side and the negative terminal to the p-side, reinforcing the built-in electric field.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Because the applied voltage has the same polarity across the depletion region as the built-in potential, the effective barrier height is given by: \[ V_{\text{eff}} = V_0 + V \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Add the applied reverse voltage to the built-in potential: \[ V_{\text{eff}} = 0.70\text{ V} + 5.30\text{ V} = 6.00\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are volts (\(\text{V}\)). The barrier height increases from \(0.70\text{ V}\) to \(6.00\text{ V}\), effectively suppressing majority carrier diffusion across the junction.

Final Answer: The effective barrier height under reverse bias is \(6.00\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q12 - Majority to minority carrier ratio in silicon

questiontext.text: A pure silicon crystal contains \(5.0 \times 10^{28}\text{ atoms m}^{-3}\) and has an intrinsic carrier concentration of \(n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3}\). The crystal is doped with phosphorus at a concentration of \(0.50\text{ ppm}\). Assuming complete donor ionization at room temperature, what is the ratio of majority carrier concentration to minority carrier concentration \(n_e / n_h\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Host atomic density: \(N_{\text{Si}} = 5.0 \times 10^{28}\text{ atoms m}^{-3}\). Doping fraction: \(0.50\text{ ppm} = 0.50 \times 10^{-6}\). Intrinsic carrier concentration: \(n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16}\text{ m}^{-3}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Phosphorus is a pentavalent donor impurity, and all donors are ionized at room temperature. Thermally generated electrons are negligibly small compared to donor-contributed electrons, so \(n_e \approx N_D\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Donor density: \[ N_D = N_{\text{Si}} \times (\text{ppm fraction}) \] Law of mass action: \[ n_e n_h = n_i^2 \implies n_h = \frac{n_i^2}{n_e} \] The ratio of majority to minority carriers is: \[ \frac{n_e}{n_h} = \frac{n_e^2}{n_i^2} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate donor concentration: \[ n_e \approx N_D = 5.0 \times 10^{28} \times (0.50 \times 10^{-6}) = 2.5 \times 10^{22}\text{ m}^{-3} \] Calculate minority hole concentration: \[ n_i^2 = (1.5 \times 10^{16})^2 = 2.25 \times 10^{32}\text{ m}^{-6} \] \[ n_h = \frac{2.25 \times 10^{32}}{2.5 \times 10^{22}} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ m}^{-3} \] Compute the ratio: \[ \frac{n_e}{n_h} = \frac{2.5 \times 10^{22}}{9.0 \times 10^9} = \frac{25}{9} \times 10^{12} \approx 2.78 \times 10^{12} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless. A ratio exceeding \(10^{12}\) quantitatively demonstrates the strong suppression of minority carriers in extrinsic semiconductors.

Final Answer: The ratio of majority carrier concentration to minority carrier concentration is \(2.78 \times 10^{12}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q13 - Ratio of reverse to forward diode resistance

questiontext.text: A silicon diode displays the following characteristics: at a reverse bias of \(V = -15.0\text{ V}\), the reverse current is \(-0.75\ \mu\text{A}\). In the forward-bias region, when the voltage is increased from \(0.70\text{ V}\) to \(0.78\text{ V}\), the forward current increases from \(12.0\text{ mA}\) to \(32.0\text{ mA}\). What is the ratio of the static reverse resistance to the dynamic forward resistance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reverse bias: \(V_r = -15.0\text{ V}\), \(I_r = -0.75\ \mu\text{A} = -0.75 \times 10^{-6}\text{ A}\). Forward bias: \(V_1 = 0.70\text{ V}\), \(V_2 = 0.78\text{ V}\), \(I_1 = 12.0\text{ mA}\), \(I_2 = 32.0\text{ mA}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Static reverse resistance is determined using Ohm's law from the operating point values, while forward resistance is the dynamic incremental resistance \(\Delta V / \Delta I\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Static reverse resistance: \[ R_r = \frac{|V_r|}{|I_r|} \] Dynamic forward resistance: \[ r_f = \frac{\Delta V_f}{\Delta I_f} \] Ratio: \[ \text{Ratio} = \frac{R_r}{r_f} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate static reverse resistance \(R_r\): \[ R_r = \frac{15.0\text{ V}}{0.75 \times 10^{-6}\text{ A}} = 2.0 \times 10^7\ \Omega \] Calculate dynamic forward resistance \(r_f\): \[ \Delta V_f = 0.78\text{ V} - 0.70\text{ V} = 0.08\text{ V} \] \[ \Delta I_f = 32.0\text{ mA} - 12.0\text{ mA} = 20.0\text{ mA} = 20.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A} = 0.020\text{ A} \] \[ r_f = \frac{0.08\text{ V}}{0.020\text{ A}} = 4.0\ \Omega \] Calculate the ratio: \[ \frac{R_r}{r_f} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^7\ \Omega}{4.0\ \Omega} = 5.0 \times 10^6 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless. The factor of \(5.0 \times 10^6\) confirms the highly non-linear, unidirectional rectifying nature of the p-n junction diode.

Final Answer: The ratio of static reverse resistance to dynamic forward resistance is \(5.0 \times 10^6\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q14 - Peak inverse voltage in full wave rectifier

questiontext.text: In a centre-tapped transformer full-wave rectifier, the total rms voltage across the entire secondary winding is \(28.28\text{ V}\) (where \(20\sqrt{2}\text{ V} \approx 28.28\text{ V}\)). The diodes used are non-ideal silicon diodes, each having a forward threshold cut-in voltage drop of \(0.70\text{ V}\). What is the peak inverse voltage (PIV) that appears across each non-conducting diode during its non-conducting half-cycle?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total secondary rms voltage: \(V_{\text{sec,rms}} = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ V} \approx 28.28\text{ V}\). The secondary has a symmetrical centre tap. Diode forward threshold voltage: \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The centre tap is at reference ground potential (\(0\text{ V}\)). At peak conduction of diode \(D_1\), terminal A is at positive peak \(+V_m\) and terminal B is at negative peak \(-V_m\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Peak voltage across total secondary: \[ V_{\text{total,peak}} = \sqrt{2} \times V_{\text{sec,rms}} = \sqrt{2} \times (20\sqrt{2}\text{ V}) = 40.0\text{ V} \] Peak voltage of each half relative to centre tap: \[ V_m = \frac{V_{\text{total,peak}}}{2} = 20.0\text{ V} \] During peak conduction of \(D_1\), the potential of the common cathode terminal is: \[ V_{\text{cathode}} = V_m - V_0 \] The anode of non-conducting diode \(D_2\) is connected to terminal B at potential: \[ V_{\text{anode}} = -V_m \] The peak reverse voltage (PIV) across \(D_2\) is: \[ PIV = V_{\text{cathode}} - V_{\text{anode}} = (V_m - V_0) - (-V_m) = 2 V_m - V_0 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \(V_m = 20.0\text{ V}\) and \(V_0 = 0.70\text{ V}\): \[ PIV = 2(20.0\text{ V}) - 0.70\text{ V} = 40.0\text{ V} - 0.70\text{ V} = 39.3\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are volts (\(\text{V}\)). The result \(39.3\text{ V}\) accurately reflects the non-ideal barrier potential reduction from the theoretical \(2 V_m = 40.0\text{ V}\).

Final Answer: The peak inverse voltage across each non-conducting diode is \(39.3\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q15 - Maximum threshold wavelength for semiconductor band gap

questiontext.text: The energy band gap of silicon at room temperature is \(E_g = 1.12\text{ eV}\). Taking Planck's constant as \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\), the speed of light as \(c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\), and \(1\text{ eV} = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\), what is the maximum wavelength of light that can excite an electron from the valence band to the conduction band in silicon?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Energy band gap of silicon: \(E_g = 1.12\text{ eV}\). Planck's constant: \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\). Speed of light: \(c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Electronic charge conversion: \(1\text{ eV} = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Photoexcitation requires the incident photon energy to be at least equal to the band gap: \(h \nu \ge E_g\). The maximum wavelength corresponds to the minimum threshold energy \(E = E_g\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Photon energy-wavelength relation: \[ E_g = \frac{h c}{\lambda_{\text{max}}} \implies \lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{h c}{E_g} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Convert band gap energy to joules: \[ E_g = 1.12 \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 1.792 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} \] Calculate the product \(h c\): \[ h c = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s} \times 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1} = 1.989 \times 10^{-25}\text{ J m} \] Compute maximum wavelength: \[ \lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{1.989 \times 10^{-25}\text{ J m}}{1.792 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}} \approx 1.1099 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m} \approx 1.11 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units are metres (\(\text{m}\)), corresponding to \(1110\text{ nm}\) in the near-infrared region. Photons with wavelengths longer than \(1.11\ \mu\text{m}\) do not possess sufficient energy to bridge the silicon band gap.

Final Answer: The maximum wavelength capable of exciting electrons across the silicon band gap is \(1.11 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SEMICONDUCTOR_ELECTRONICS_MCQ_Q01 - Thermal generation and movement of holes

questiontext.text:
In an intrinsic semiconductor such as silicon at a temperature \( T > 0\text{ K} \), thermal excitation leads to conduction through both free electrons and holes. Consider the microscopic events involved in the thermal generation and apparent movement of a hole through the crystal lattice:

(I) Thermal energy breaks a covalent bond in the crystal lattice, releasing a free conduction electron.
(II) A vacancy with an effective positive charge, known as a hole, is created at the site of the broken bond.
(III) A valence electron in a neighbouring intact covalent bond acquires energy and jumps into the vacant site.
(IV) The original vacancy is filled, and a new vacancy is formed at the neighbouring bond site from which the electron hopped.
(V) Under an external applied electric field, continuous sequential hopping of bound valence electrons creates a macroscopic hole current moving towards the negative potential.

Which of the following represents the correct chronological sequence of these events?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In an intrinsic semiconductor, electrical conduction involves two independent charge carriers: free electrons in the conduction band and holes in the valence band. A hole represents an electron deficiency (vacancy) in a covalent bond that behaves as an apparent mobile particle with an effective positive electronic charge \( +q \).

Step 2: Sequential Analysis of Physical Events
The microscopic process unfolds in the following physical order:
First, at finite temperatures (\( T > 0\text{ K} \)), thermal energy imparted to the lattice vibrates the silicon atoms, occasionally supplying enough energy to break a covalent bond and release a conduction electron.
Second, the departure of the thermally excited electron leaves behind an unoccupied covalent bond with an unneutralised positive core charge, forming a hole at that specific lattice site.
Third, an adjacent bound valence electron in a neighboring bond can transition into this unoccupied site without becoming a free conduction electron.
Fourth, once this valence electron occupies the initial vacant site, the initial bond becomes intact, but a new vacancy is simultaneously produced at the donor bond site, resulting in the apparent displacement of the hole.
Fifth, when an external electric field is applied, these successive jumps of bound valence electrons occur preferentially towards the positive potential, causing the apparent vacancy (hole) to migrate towards the negative potential and constitute a steady hole current.

Step 3: Verification of Sequence Logic
A hole cannot move before it is generated, and valence electron hopping into a site requires a pre-existing vacancy. Furthermore, directed macroscopic current is the cumulative result of directional hopping under an applied field. Hence, the logical progression flows naturally from initial thermal ionisation to lattice-site hopping, followed by apparent motion, and finally field-driven drift.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is: Thermal bond breaking and electron release → Creation of a vacancy (hole) → Valence electron jump from an adjacent bond → Apparent movement of the hole to the adjacent site → Macroscopic hole drift under an applied electric field.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SEMICONDUCTOR_ELECTRONICS_MCQ_Q02 - Stages in formation of pn junction

questiontext.text:
When a p-type semiconductor wafer is partially transformed to synthesize an integrated metallurgical junction with an n-type semiconductor, several physical processes occur to establish an unbiased p-n junction. Arrange the following stages in their correct logical sequence:

(I) Due to concentration gradients, majority holes diffuse from the p-side to the n-side and majority electrons diffuse from the n-side to the p-side, setting up a diffusion current.
(II) Diffusing carriers recombine near the interface, leaving behind immobile ionised donor cores on the n-side and immobile ionised acceptor cores on the p-side, creating a space-charge depletion region.
(III) An internal barrier electric field builds up across the depletion region, directed from the positive space-charge (n-side) towards the negative space-charge (p-side).
(IV) The electric field sweeps minority carriers across the junction, initiating a drift current directed opposite to the diffusion current.
(V) As the space-charge layer widens, the drift current increases until it equals the diffusion current, establishing dynamic equilibrium with zero net current.

Which of the following gives the correct chronological order?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The formation of a p-n junction is governed by two opposing carrier transport mechanisms: diffusion due to carrier concentration gradients, and drift driven by the induced internal space-charge electric field.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Junction Formation
1. Initially, a steep concentration gradient exists across the metallurgical junction because hole concentration is much greater on the p-side and electron concentration is much greater on the n-side. Consequently, majority holes diffuse from p to n and majority electrons diffuse from n to p.
2. As electrons diffuse across to the p-side, they leave uncompensated positive donor ions fixed in the n-lattice. Similarly, holes diffusing to the n-side leave uncompensated negative acceptor ions fixed in the p-lattice. This creates a region stripped of mobile carriers called the depletion layer.
3. The presence of positive ions on the n-edge and negative ions on the p-edge produces an internal electric field pointing from n to p.
4. This internal electric field exerts forces on minority carriers that enter the depletion zone (electrons on the p-side and holes on the n-side), driving them across the boundary and generating a drift current in the opposite direction to diffusion current.
5. As diffusion continues, the depletion region widens, intensifying the electric field and increasing the drift current. Eventually, the drift current precisely balances the diffusion current, leading to an equilibrium barrier potential \( V_0 \) with zero net current across the terminal leads.

Step 3: Verification of Sequence Logic
Diffusion is the primary driving mechanism that uncovers immobile ion cores. These immobile cores are the direct source of the electric field. In turn, the electric field is the prerequisite for carrier drift, which grows until equilibrium balance is attained.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is: Diffusion of majority charge carriers → Space-charge depletion layer formation → Generation of internal electric field → Initiation of minority carrier drift → Attainment of dynamic equilibrium with equal diffusion and drift currents.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_SEMICONDUCTOR_ELECTRONICS_MCQ_Q03 - Operation of rectifier with capacitor filter

questiontext.text:
In a full-wave rectifier circuit equipped with a parallel capacitor input filter across a load resistor \( R_L \), arrange the following stages in their correct chronological sequence during one complete steady-state operational cycle:

(I) The rising input alternating voltage applied to the conducting diode exceeds the residual voltage across the capacitor, forward-biasing the diode.
(II) The forward-biased diode conducts current heavily, charging the capacitor up to the peak voltage of the rectified sinusoid.
(III) The rectified input sinusoid peaks and starts falling, causing the diode to become reverse-biased as its anode potential drops below the capacitor potential.
(IV) With the diode cut off, the capacitor discharges stored charge through the load resistor \( R_L \) with a rate governed by the time constant \( R_L C \), maintaining the output voltage.
(V) In the subsequent half-cycle, the voltage across the secondary winding reverses and rises until it exceeds the falling voltage across the capacitor, switching the alternate diode on.

Which of the following represents the correct sequence?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A capacitor input filter smoothens rectified ac pulsations into a near-steady dc voltage. The diode conducts only during short intervals when the input ac transformer secondary voltage exceeds the capacitor voltage; during the remainder of the cycle, the diode remains reverse-biased and the capacitor sustains load current by discharging through \( R_L \).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Working of the Filter Cycle
1. At the beginning of the conduction period, the rectified ac voltage rising towards its peak reaches and then exceeds the decaying voltage retained across the capacitor. This makes the diode anode more positive than its cathode, establishing forward bias.
2. Once forward biased, the diode acts as a low-resistance path, allowing current to flow into both the load and the capacitor, rapidly charging the capacitor until the voltage reaches the peak rectified value \( V_{\text{peak}} \).
3. Immediately after the input wave passes through its peak, the input voltage drops below \( V_{\text{peak}} \). Because the capacitor holds the peak voltage, the cathode of the diode is at a higher potential than its anode, reverse-biasing the diode and turning it off.
4. During this cutoff period, the diode does not conduct. The capacitor delivers energy to the load resistor \( R_L \), discharging slowly with an exponential rate determined by the time constant \( \tau = R_L C \).
5. In the next half-cycle, the opposite half of the centre-tapped secondary produces an increasing positive voltage at the alternate diode. When this new pulse exceeds the declining capacitor voltage, the alternate diode is forward-biased, re-initiating the charging cycle.

Step 3: Verification of Operational Cycle
Charging to peak must precede discharging, and diode cutoff naturally occurs the instant the sinusoidal input decreases below the capacitor's peak voltage. Conduction in the alternate half-cycle can only occur once the alternate secondary voltage overcomes the remaining voltage on the capacitor.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is: Input voltage exceeding capacitor voltage → Diode conduction and capacitor charging to peak voltage → Input voltage falling below peak causing diode cutoff → Capacitor discharging through load resistor → Input voltage in next half-cycle rising to recharge capacitor.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Electrical conductivity range of semiconductor materials

questiontext.text: Based on electrical conductivity \(\sigma\), which of the following ranges correctly represents semiconductors at room temperature as classified in solid-state electronics?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Solids are classified into metals, semiconductors, and insulators based on their relative values of electrical resistivity \(\rho\) or electrical conductivity \(\sigma = 1/\rho\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Conductivity Ranges
Metals possess very high electrical conductivity, typically \(\sigma \sim 10^2\) to \(10^8\text{ S m}^{-1}\) (or resistivity \(\rho \sim 10^{-2}\) to \(10^{-8}\ \Omega\text{ m}\)). Insulators possess extremely low electrical conductivity, typically \(\sigma \sim 10^{-11}\) to \(10^{-19}\text{ S m}^{-1}\) (or resistivity \(\rho \sim 10^{11}\) to \(10^{19}\ \Omega\text{ m}\)). Semiconductors have conductivity intermediate between metals and insulators, lying in the range \(\sigma \sim 10^5\) to \(10^{-6}\text{ S m}^{-1}\) (corresponding to resistivity \(\rho \sim 10^{-5}\) to \(10^6\ \Omega\text{ m}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The conductivity range characteristic of semiconductors is \(10^5\text{ S m}^{-1}\) to \(10^{-6}\text{ S m}^{-1}\).

Final Answer: The electrical conductivity of semiconductors lies in the range of \(10^5\text{ S m}^{-1}\) to \(10^{-6}\text{ S m}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Available energy states in silicon crystal lattice

questiontext.text: In a silicon crystal containing \(N\) atoms, each atom has four valence electrons. What are the total numbers of available energy states in the valence band and the conduction band at absolute zero?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a crystal containing \(N\) atoms of silicon or germanium, the outer shell has 4 valence electrons per atom (\(2s\) and \(2p\) electrons), giving a total of \(4N\) valence electrons. The maximum capacity of the outer shell is 8 electrons (\(2s + 6p\)), providing \(8N\) available discrete energy states.

Step 2: Band Splitting Analysis
At the interatomic equilibrium distance of the crystal lattice, these \(8N\) states split into two separate bands separated by an energy gap \(E_g\). The lower band, consisting of \(4N\) states, is completely filled by the \(4N\) valence electrons at \(0\text{ K}\) and is called the valence band. The upper band, also consisting of \(4N\) states, is completely empty at \(0\text{ K}\) and is called the conduction band.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the valence band and the conduction band contain \(4N\) energy states each.

Final Answer: The valence band contains \(4N\) states and the conduction band contains \(4N\) states.

answer.text: \(8N\) states in the valence band and \(4N\) states in the conduction band
\(4N\) states in the valence band and \(4N\) states in the conduction band
\(2N\) states in the valence band and \(6N\) states in the conduction band
\(4N\) states in the valence band and \(8N\) states in the conduction band

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Behavior of pure semiconductor at absolute zero

questiontext.text: At a temperature of \(T = 0\text{ K}\), how does an ideal intrinsic semiconductor behave with respect to electrical conduction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In an intrinsic semiconductor, electrical conduction requires charge carriers (free electrons in the conduction band and holes in the valence band), which are generated through thermal excitation across the energy band gap \(E_g\).

Step 2: Evaluation at Zero Kelvin
At \(T = 0\text{ K}\), zero thermal energy is available to promote electrons across the energy gap \(E_g\). Consequently, all \(4N\) valence electrons remain bound in the valence band, rendering the valence band completely filled and the conduction band completely empty.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
With no free charge carriers available in the conduction band or vacancies in the valence band, the material behaves as a perfect insulator.

Final Answer: At \(0\text{ K}\), an intrinsic semiconductor behaves as an insulator because its valence band is completely filled and its conduction band is completely empty.

answer.text: As a metallic conductor, due to spontaneous overlap of the valence and conduction bands
As a material with high hole conductivity in the valence band
As an insulator, with a completely filled valence band and an empty conduction band
As a superconductor, with zero electrical resistivity

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Identification of trivalent acceptor impurity atoms

questiontext.text: Which of the following elements acts as an acceptor impurity when doped into a pure silicon crystal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dopants in tetravalent silicon or germanium are categorized based on their valency. Trivalent elements (valency 3) create holes and act as acceptor impurities, producing p-type semiconductors. Pentavalent elements (valency 5) donate conduction electrons and act as donor impurities, producing n-type semiconductors.

Step 2: Evaluation of Impurity Elements
Arsenic (As), antimony (Sb), and phosphorus (P) belong to Group 15 and are pentavalent donor impurities. Boron (B), along with aluminium (Al) and indium (In), belongs to Group 13 and is a trivalent acceptor impurity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Boron is a trivalent element that accepts an electron to form a hole, acting as an acceptor impurity.

Final Answer: Boron acts as an acceptor impurity in silicon.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q05 - Nature of charges forming diode depletion region

questiontext.text: What constitutes the space-charge depletion region formed on either side of an unbiased p-n junction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When a p-n junction forms, concentration gradients cause electrons to diffuse from the n-side to the p-side and holes to diffuse from the p-side to the n-side.

Step 2: Analysis of Space Charge Layer
As electrons leave the n-side, they expose uncompensated, fixed positive donor ions. As holes leave the p-side, they expose uncompensated, fixed negative acceptor ions. Because the free carriers in this layer have recombined or diffused away, this space-charge region is depleted of mobile charge carriers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The depletion layer consists of fixed, immobile positive donor ions on the n-region side and fixed, immobile negative acceptor ions on the p-region side, completely devoid of free charge carriers.

Final Answer: The depletion region consists of immobile positive donor ions on the n-side and immobile negative acceptor ions on the p-side, devoid of free charge carriers.

answer.text: Immobile positive donor ions on the n-side and immobile negative acceptor ions on the p-side, devoid of free charge carriers
Free conduction electrons on the p-side and free holes on the n-side
Neutral semiconductor atoms with all covalent bonds intact
Accumulation of equal numbers of mobile electrons and mobile holes

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q06 - Output frequency of full wave rectifier circuit

questiontext.text: If an alternating input voltage of mains frequency \(50\text{ Hz}\) is fed into a full-wave rectifier using a centre-tapped transformer, what is the fundamental ripple frequency of the output voltage across the load resistor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
